# Lab 18.10: VPC Service Controls

## What We Are Going to Do
Put BigQuery inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter and see a query from outside the perimeter blocked. This needs a Google Cloud organisation.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Find your access policy.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com
ORG_ID=$(gcloud projects get-ancestors $PROJECT_ID --format="value(id)" | tail -1)
gcloud access-context-manager policies list --organization=$ORG_ID
export POLICY=&lt;POLICY_NUMBER&gt;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Create a perimeter in dry-run mode first.** **Security → VPC Service Controls → New perimeter**:
   - **Name**: `bq_lab_perimeter`, **Type**: Regular, **Enforcement**: **Dry run**
   - **Projects**: `bq-course-lab`
   - **Restricted services**: BigQuery API, Cloud Storage API

3. **[Console] Read the dry-run violations.** Run a query from Cloud Shell, then open **Logs Explorer** with `protoPayload.metadata.dryRun=true`. The query would have been blocked.

4. **[CLI] Enforce the perimeter.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud access-context-manager perimeters dry-run enforce bq_lab_perimeter --policy=$POLICY</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[CLI] Test from outside.** From Cloud Shell (outside the perimeter):


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab18.sales'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   It fails with **Request is prohibited by organization's policy**. Copying data to a project outside the perimeter is also blocked.

6. **[CLI] Delete the perimeter** so the rest of the course works.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud access-context-manager perimeters delete bq_lab_perimeter --policy=$POLICY</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Perimeter | Protects BigQuery and Storage APIs |
| Dry run | Shows what would be blocked |
| Enforced | Outside access and exfiltration blocked |
| Requirement | An organisation |
